h: Gems, Dickens and a lane booked
p: Holborn is full of surprising corners. Hatton Garden, a few minutes' walk away, has been London's jewellery quarter for generations, with shop windows glittering with diamonds and gold. Leather Lane, running parallel, hosts a lively weekday street market famous for its lunchtime food stalls. Both are great places to while away an hour before heading to the lanes.

Literature fans can visit the Charles Dickens Museum on Doughty Street, in the house where Dickens lived and wrote Oliver Twist. The Hunterian Museum at the Royal College of Surgeons on Lincoln's Inn Fields reopened in recent years and displays an extraordinary collection of anatomical specimens, which might not be for the squeamish but is a real one-off.

For your visit, bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly check. Book ahead, especially for Friday and Saturday nights, and think about two lanes if you've got a group of more than six, so nobody is left waiting too long between turns. Swapping teams halfway through stops anyone hogging the glory.

Getting here is easy. Holborn station is on the Central and Piccadilly lines, and Chancery Lane and Tottenham Court Road aren't far either, so you can get in from almost anywhere in London. It's the sort of area where you can easily build a whole day, with museums, markets and history in the daytime and a bit of bowling to round it off.
